topic: Webmux: Like Tmux, but for the Browser

key_points: Primary source: WebMux is a browser-based remote workspace for persistent terminal and desktop sessions
Started as tmux-on-a-jump-box: a shared, scrollable wall of SSH and mosh terminals
Now also brings VNC, RDP, and optional tmux-backed coding-agent sessions into the same web interface
2D tiled terminal workspace with scrollable CSS Grid of fixed-size terminals; click '+' placeholders to add sessions
Full terminal emulation via xterm.js with 256-color, clickable links, 5000-line scrollback
SSH and mosh transports via node-pty with keepalive and auto-reconnect
Persistent sessions survive browser closes and server reboots; auto-reconnected on startup
Remote desktop workspace for VNC and RDP sessions with fullscreen viewing
Multi-user accounts with Argon2id password hashing; multi-viewer presence with click-to-focus
Type to All broadcast mode sends keystrokes to every open session
Keyboard terminal cycling via Ctrl+Shift+< and Ctrl+Shift+>
Two security modes: local auth (Argon2id + JWT + HTTPS) or trusted mode for isolated networks
OS service integration: launchd (macOS), systemd (Linux), Windows SCM
YAML config in ~/.config/webmux/; audit log as append-only JSONL
45 GitHub stars, TypeScript, created 2026-03-07, 15 releases (latest v1.3.3 2026-08-28)

angles: WebMux is a self-hosted 'tmux for the browser' that unifies SSH/mosh terminals, VNC/RDP desktops, and coding-agent sessions in one tiled web workspace
Differentiation: unlike single-session tools (ttyd/gotty), WebMux is a full persistent multi-session multiplexer with 2D tiling, presence, and broadcast mode
The 'jump box' origin story: built for a shared scrollable wall of SSH/mosh terminals, then expanded to remote desktops and agent sessions
Security posture: Argon2id + JWT + HTTPS local auth vs trusted mode for isolated networks - relevant for self-hosters
Practical review angle: setup, build/run, service install, and whether it's a viable ttyd/gotty/Guacamole alternative
HN reception was lukewarm (26 points, 2 comments) - one commenter questioned the use case, another wanted demos/screenshots
